card.name: Tor-Tor
card.era: Ancient; some accounts estimate from the 13th century
card.tagline: Batak ritual dance of stomping feet and gondang music
card.profile: Tortor (Tor-Tor) is a traditional Batak dance from North Sumatra, originally a sacred ritual dance performed at funerals, healing ceremonies and other Batak ceremonies (Wikipedia). For the Batak it carries cultural and spiritual value, expressing hopes and prayers; performance types include Tortor Sombasomba (worship), Simonangmonang (victory) and Habonaran (truth). The name comes from the sound of dancers stomping their feet on a Batak house's floorboards. It is accompanied by gondang musical instruments, with dancers wearing ulos cloth; movements are simple - hands waving up and down and feet stamping to the rhythm - and the host (hasuhutan) opens with a request to the gondang musicians.
card.insight: Tortor functions as a medium of communication: through its movements, interaction occurs between ceremony participants, with songs appealing to God and ancestral spirits for safety, prosperity and blessing (Wikipedia; Trekking Orangutan Sumatra).
card.image_significance: Batak ancestral ritual dance. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — N. Sumatra (Batak), Indonesia.
